name: Maltese

ancestors.notes: Descent from Siculo-Arabic (Maghrebi Arabic of Sicily).
Sicilian superstrate: absorbed prestige layer, large share of the lexicon.
Italian superstrate: further Romance vocabulary and phonemes.
English adstrate: colonial and modern loanwords.

notes: Maltese, the only Semitic language written in the Latin script and official EU language. Evolved from Siculo-Arabic. Digraph għ represents pharyngeal fricative, h is silent. Ċ and ġ are retroflex-palatal affricates. Extensive lexical borrowing from Sicilian/Italian and English.

sources.author: Lucas, Christopher; Čéplö, Slavomír
sources.title: Maltese. In Lucas & Manfredi (eds.), Arabic and Contact-Induced Change, 265-302
sources.notes: §3.1.1-3.1.2, read in full. Table 2 (p. 270) gives the consonant inventory in Maltese orthography: ⟨p b t d k q⟩ plosives with ⟨q⟩ the glottal stop, ⟨z ċ ġ⟩ affricates (⟨z⟩ covering both ts and dz, p. 269), ⟨f v s ż x ħ⟩ fricatives, ⟨m n r l w j⟩. p. 271: ⟨għ⟩ has no phonetic correlate or lengthens the neighbouring vowel, and ⟨għ⟩+⟨h⟩ is realised ħː; ⟨h⟩ has merged with ħ in codas (ikrah /ɪkˈrɐħ/) and sporadically in onsets, and is otherwise lost. p. 273: five short vowel qualities ɪ ɛ ɐ ɔ ʊ for ⟨i e a o u⟩ and six long ones iː ɪː ɛː ɐː ɔː uː for ⟨i ie e a o u⟩, plus seven diphthongs. Three disagreements with this map, recorded and not changed: the map gives ⟨għ⟩ = ʕ where the source has it silent or vowel-lengthening in Standard Maltese (a pharyngeal only in conservative dialects); the map's notes call ⟨ċ ġ⟩ retroflex-palatal where the source has plain postalveolar tʃ dʒ; and the map has ⟨h⟩ silent everywhere where the source has it as ħ in codas. The map's ⟨ie⟩ = ɪə is also given as long ɪː by the source.
